## Why This Is Asked

- Multilingual encoders (XLM-R), zero/few-shot adaptation
- Drift & fairness monitoring per language

## Code Example
```javascript
// Example: simple adapter switch in inference path
function infer(message, lang, adapters){
  const base = encoder.encode(message, lang)
  const rep = adapters[lang]?.apply(base) ?? base
  return classifier.predict(rep)
}
```

- How to ensure explainability remains stable with new intents?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a real-time, privacy-preserving NLP system that handles code-switch scenarios common in global enterprise chat, with practical latency and drift considerations.

## Key Concepts

- Code-switch NLP and language segmentation
- Per-language encoders + shared extraction head
- Privacy-preserving tenant isolation
- Real-time latency targets and model quantization
- Drift detection, canary rollout, rollback strategies

## Code Example

```python
# sketch: routing by language segment
def route_segment(token_seq):
    lang = detect_language(token_seq)
    encoder = ENCODERS[lang]
    embedding = encoder.encode(token_seq)
    return embedding
```

- How would you evaluate cross-language drift and decide when to rollback?
